title: Correlation and Statistical Relationships
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of correlation and statistical relationships and identify its main inputs, outputs or constraints.
Apply testing correlation in a minimal example and state the expected result before checking it.
Test one relevant edge, missing or failure case and describe a limitation of the result.

content.intro: Correlation and Statistical Relationships is part of Probability, Statistical Inference, and Experiments. Start with testing correlation and connect it to the worked example and expected result.
content.why_it_matters: Statistical conclusions depend on data quality, design, assumptions and uncertainty, not just the value returned by one function.

content_blocks.title: Why this matters
content_blocks.text: Statistical conclusions depend on data quality, design, assumptions and uncertainty, not just the value returned by one function. The example is intentionally small so you can predict its result before checking it in a local R session.

items.title: Testing Correlation

content_blocks.title: Work through it
content_blocks.text: State the question and assumptions, calculate a small example, and explain uncertainty or a limitation in context. Change one input or condition at a time, compare the observed result with your prediction, and write down one limitation.

content_blocks.title: R example: Correlation and Statistical Relationships
content_blocks.code:
# Lesson 149: Correlation and Statistical Relationships
measurements <- c(4, 6, 8)
mean(measurements)

content_blocks.title: Common pitfall
content_blocks.text: Do not treat a syntactically plausible example as proof of correctness. For correlation and statistical relationships, check the input type, missing/empty cases, output shape, and domain assumptions.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating a p-value, coefficient or score as a complete conclusion.
common_mistakes.why: Study design, assumptions, effect size and uncertainty shape interpretation.
common_mistakes.fix: State the question, inspect diagnostics and report uncertainty and limitations.

common_mistakes.problem: Using test data during feature selection or tuning.
common_mistakes.why: This leaks information and leads to an overly optimistic evaluation.
common_mistakes.fix: Separate training, validation and final test roles before modeling.

common_mistakes.problem: Reporting a model without comparing it with a baseline.
common_mistakes.why: Complexity does not guarantee useful performance.
common_mistakes.fix: Evaluate an appropriate simple baseline with task-relevant metrics.
